title: Region Stabilizer with probabilistic capacity steering
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: During cross-region surges we see P95 latency spikes in secondary regions caused by abrupt hedging and a cascade of fallbacks that overload smaller regional pools. Current routing is deterministic: latency-first then geo-pin, with blunt circuit breakers that tripped regions offline. That results in user-visible latency regressions and customer incidents.
goal: Design and implement a Region Stabilizer that uses SLO-weighted probabilistic steering, capacity hint tokens, and soft quarantine lanes to reduce cascade failures. The policy should bias routing toward low-latency regions while preventing abrupt load transfers to capacity-limited regions and providing graceful degradation with circuit-breaker hysteresis.
acceptance_criteria: New routing policy deployed behind a feature flag and default-off for 2-week canary
P95 tail latency improves in simulated 2x surge tests vs current deterministic steering by >=15% in affected regions
Fallback-induced overloads on small regions reduced (peak GPU util drop >=20%) in chaos tests
SLOs: region-level error budget burn rate remains within target for 4 consecutive runs of synthetic traffic profiles
Operational controls exposed in Console: per-region capacity weight, quarantine threshold, circuit breaker time constants
implementation_notes: Routing algorithm: compute SLO-adjusted score = base_latency_score * (1 + slack_multiplier) * capacity_factor. Convert scores into probabilistic weights using softmax with temperature tuned per region size.

Capacity hints: each region emits a capacity_token count (reservoir) representing concurrent tokenized slots. Steering reduces probability to regions with tokens below quarantine_threshold and increases soft-failback to larger pools.

Circuit breakers: migrate from binary trips to graded states (green/amber/quarantine/red) with separate thresholds for latency, error-rate, and capacity depletion. Amber state triggers probability damping, quarantine state forces probabilistic routing with increased temperature to favor other regions.
Geo pinning: maintain per-customer affinity with exponential decay. If local region enters amber/quarantine, affinity decays faster to reduce immediate reroutes.
Telemetry: new metrics (region_capacity_tokens, route_weight, region_state, route_probability) instrumented at gateway layer and exported to metric store and tracing.
Backward compatibility: policy initially lives in steering service behind a flag; existing deterministic fallback remains available as an escape hatch.
Data model: no schema changes to request envelopes; steering uses side-channel health signals and metrics.
PRs: implementation split into steering-core, tokens-protocol, and console-controls repos for parallel reviews.
Estimated lift: ~6 engineer-weeks across infra, serving, and console engineers; initial rollout in 2 phases (canary -> opt-in customers -> default)
rollout_plan: Feature flag gated rollout: enable in staging cluster and run synthetic surge scenarios
Canary: enable for 5% of traffic in us-west primary for 48h; monitor p50/p95/p99, error rates, region_capacity_tokens
Expand to 20% after stability checks and run inter-region chaos tests (link to runbook)
Opt-in beta for two heavy customers to validate affinity decay and local latency impact
Default enablement after 2-week canary with rollback hooks and observability dashboards
Post-rollout: 1-week close monitoring and a retrospective to validate acceptance criteria
telemetry_and_alerting: New alerts: region_state->red for >2m, region_capacity_tokens below 10% for >5m, route_probability shift >50% within 1m window
Dashboards: per-region SLO burn charts, steering decisions heatmap (origin region -> chosen region), token reservoir visualization
Tracing: annotate hedged requests with chosen scoring and capacity_token values for post-mortem analysis
SLO experiments: run synthetic traffic with controlled tail latencies to measure sensitivity and adjust slack_multiplier
test_plan: Unit tests for softmax weighting and temperature tuning logic
Integration tests: simulate 3-region topology with controlled capacity signals and validate probabilistic distribution
Chaos test: sudden loss of primary region capacity while secondary region is at 60% utilization; measure percent of requests routed into third region vs previous policy
Load test: ramp to 3x baseline to observe circuit-breaker hysteresis and quarantine behavior
Customer regression: test per-customer affinity across region transitions to ensure session continuity
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: probabilistic routing may increase request variance for a small subset of users. Mitigation: keep geo-affinity decay conservative and add per-customer pin override for enterprise customers.
Risk: incorrect capacity token instrumentation could steer traffic incorrectly. Mitigation: shadow-mode validation for tokens for 48h before enabling steering decisions.
Risk: new alerts noisy. Mitigation: initial alert thresholds set wide and refined during canary; provide suppression knobs.
Risk: UX complexity in Console. Mitigation: expose only three primary controls (capacity weight, quarantine threshold, enable flag) and advanced controls under expert mode.
Risk: unforeseen interactions with autoscaler. Mitigation: coordinate with infra team and add dependency ticket ENG-142690 (autoscaler-compat)
